sections.h2: Quick-sale paths for a Frisco home
sections.html:
A Frisco seller can take a cash purchase, list with an agent, or sell to an investor. The mean home value was near $476,000 in 2020, so a house here is a large asset and the comparison between offers deserves care.

Frisco draws many movers, which gives sellers of updated homes a ready pool of financed buyers. A cash offer suits a different seller: someone relocating, settling an estate, facing a deadline or holding a house whose repairs would cost time and money before listing.

  • Cash route: fewer contingencies and a closing date you can often set, at a price below a fully prepared listing.
  • Listing route: broader exposure, plus commission, showings and possible repair requests.
  • Hybrid route: list first, then take a cash offer if showings stall.

Whichever you pick, request a written net sheet showing payoff, taxes, fees and the amount you receive.

Frisco lies in west central Collin County and east central Denton County, about 25 miles north of downtown Dallas. Your tax bill and deed show which county applies to your lot.

Frisco ISD is the main district, with 63,533 students enrolled in 2020. Parts of the city also fall in Lewisville ISD, Little Elm ISD and Prosper ISD, so check the district for your exact address before advertising. About 34 percent of residents rent among 73,633 housing units, so a Frisco seller may also be selling to an investor or landlord.

New homes compete with resale houses here. The city issued 2,373 residential building permits in fiscal 2021, so price a resale house against new builds nearby, not just against old sales. If your house backs onto a development site, ask the city planning staff what is planned before you list.

sections.h2: What to point out in a listing
sections.html:
Parks, trails and schools carry a Frisco listing. The city has 1,545 acres of developed parks, 24 baseball fields, 35 soccer fields, six tennis courts and a recreation center. DFW Airport and Love Field are within about a half hour's drive, and the average commute was about 29 minutes in 2020.

Voters approved a $345 million bond authorization in May 2019 for public safety, streets, public works, the library and parks. Street and park projects can change traffic near a house, so a buyer may ask what is planned near your lot. The city engineering staff can share the capital project list.

  • Name the nearest park or trail and the school zone.
  • Note proximity to the tollway or Highway 121 if it applies.
  • Keep records of recent updates, since buyers compare homes against newer builds.

A Frisco bill can carry several line items. A house in Collin County and Frisco ISD pays the city, the county, the school district and Collin College, while Denton County parcels pay that county instead.

DateWhat happens
January 1Value and the year's lien are fixed
October 1Bills are mailed
January 31Unpaid tax turns delinquent

The closing agent settles the current year from your proceeds. Homestead exemptions on a Frisco bill have included a senior exemption of $80,000 and a 10 percent homestead exemption, but amounts change, so ask the Collin or Denton County tax office about the exemptions on your current bill.

Exemptions stay with the property. The buyer applies for new ones, while the school tax ceiling for an older owner can follow them to another Texas homestead.

  • A homestead appraisal cap limits yearly increases after the first exemption year.
  • Owners with a disability rating receive relief from $5,000 to $12,000 by rating, and a 100 percent rating can exempt the entire homestead.

The Collin Central Appraisal District or its Denton counterpart can show the exemptions on your account.

sections.h2: Inherited, behind on payments or leased
sections.html:
Each case changes the paperwork more than the price. Heirs can compare the small estate affidavit, the affidavit of heirship and the muniment of title, and your title company will say which one it accepts.

For a loan in default, a lender may sue for a deficiency within two years after a foreclosure sale. Selling first can avoid that exposure.

For a leased house, the process runs through notice and court steps, though many buyers simply take the lease. Tell each buyer what applies before they bid, because a surprise discovered late is the usual reason an offer drops.

The Collin County or Denton County clerk files the deed, depending on the parcel. The instrument must carry an acknowledgment from an authorized officer.

Your closing agent handles the filing and the fee, so read the settlement statement the day before you sign.

  • Bring photo ID to closing.
  • Have your payoff letter and tax statements ready.
  • Confirm who signs for any trust or estate.

Two bids with the same headline can leave you with very different checks. Read for the items that move money: who pays for the title policy, whether the buyer wants a credit for repairs after walking through, how many days you have to move out, and whether the earnest money is refundable. A bid that looks lower but has no strings can beat a higher one that leaves room to renegotiate.

Ask who the buyer is and how they have paid in the past. A buyer with funds ready needs no financing contingency, and that is the real value of cash. Ask for a copy of the proof of funds, and ask the title company to confirm that the earnest money has arrived once the contract is signed.

If anything is unclear, bring the contract to a real estate attorney before signing. A short review costs little compared with a sale that falls apart over a missed clause.

Start by deciding how much work you are willing to do. Newer homes nearby set the standard buyers compare against, so fresh paint, clean floors and working fixtures help even when you sell as-is. Skip big renovations unless an agent shows you the return.

Gather the deed, a payoff letter, tax statements and any receipts for the roof, air conditioning or plumbing. Then ask each buyer for the same things in writing: price, closing date, who pays title and recording fees, and whether the price holds after their walkthrough. Compare the net amounts side by side. If you need to stay in the house after closing, ask for a short leaseback and put the dates in the contract.

faqs.q: Is Frisco in Collin County or Denton County?
faqs.a: Both. The city lies in west central Collin County and east central Denton County, so your tax bill and deed show which applies.

faqs.q: How quickly can I close on a cash offer in Frisco?
faqs.a: A clear title closes fastest, and the buyer should give you a date in writing.

faqs.q: Do Frisco tax exemptions go to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. The buyer files fresh applications.

faqs.q: Can a Frisco house with a loan still be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The lender is paid at the closing table and the balance is yours. Ask your servicer for a payoff letter.

faqs.q: Where is a Frisco deed recorded?
faqs.a: With the Collin or Denton County clerk, whichever county holds the lot.
